items.stem: In an EMS, what is the difference between an environmental aspect and an environmental impact?

options.text: The aspect is the element that interacts with the environment; the impact is the resulting change
options.rationale: Correct: e.g. the aspect is 'solvent emission'; the impact is 'air quality degradation'.

options.text: They are two words for the same thing
options.rationale: They are distinct: cause (aspect) versus effect (impact).

options.text: The impact is the activity and the aspect is the result

options.rationale: Aspects cover normal, abnormal and emergency conditions.

items.explanation: Correct: e.g. the aspect is 'solvent emission'; the impact is 'air quality degradation'.

items.stem: Which TWO activities belong to the 'Check' stage of the EMS Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: internal audit evaluates conformity and effectiveness in the Check stage.

options.text: Monitoring and measuring key environmental parameters
options.rationale: Correct: monitoring results are a core Check activity.
Setting objectives is part of Plan, not Check.

options.text: Implementing operational controls on the shop floor
options.rationale: Carrying out controls is part of Do, not Check.

items.stem: Which environmental objective is well formed for an EMS?

options.text: Reduce solvent use by 15% within 12 months, owned by the production manager
options.rationale: Correct: it is measurable, time-bound and has a clear owner.

options.text: Try to be more environmentally friendly
options.rationale: It is vague, unmeasurable and has no owner or timeframe.

options.text: Comply with all laws at all times
options.rationale: This is a baseline obligation, not an improvement objective with a target.
It names an action without a measurable target, date or owner.

items.explanation: Correct: it is measurable, time-bound and has a clear owner.
